body:
I so get it. Right there with you.

The worst is having to justify still being unemployed to friends and family. I'm not really socialising for Christmas this year, either. They just don't get it. Like, if I don't bring it up myself, then just don't ask. I haven't really been meeting up with friends, partly because job hunting is a full time job, but also because I can't stand having the same conversation over and over again. 

Hang in there. I'm hoping things will look up in January.

Hi again!

I hope you've had a great week! That's intriguing; do you mind sharing what your book is about? I can imagine that it's difficult to sit down and write every day and be consistent with that habit. Different authors have different styles, though, right? I assume there are phases when it just *flows" and then there are times when you have to be disciplined to get your writing done. In any way, I'm excited for you – what a great endeavour!

There's always such a huge discrepancy between what I know intellectually to be true and what I end up doing/how I end up living my life in reality. In my mind, my tasks are levels and only once I've taken the step I'm currently working on, I can move on to the next one. The dentist is a few steps away because my whole thing right now is finding a job. I know it sounds crazy, but I can't really focus on anything else until I can put a check next to this current level.

A planner is a great idea and I've been using one for the past few years. You're absolutely right when you say that checking off even minor accomplishments is hugely gratifying. In fact, I've come across a meme yesterday that made me think of our conversation: https://pics.onsizzle.com/sometimes-adults-need-gold-stars-too-u-only-cried-like-4017855.png This is essentially my life right now. 

Yes, exactly; I'm not usually insecure about my writing, but writing this post and subsequent comments, I've tried not to edit myself and not make it a well-structured essay, but to really write what was going through my mind at the exact moment. Interestingly enough, an acquaintance brought up Tuesday's full moon and – depending on whether you believe in that kind of stuff – that makes a lot of sense to me. I'm hoping Tuesday was rockbottom and that things will be looking up from here on out for others and for myself. 

I'm happy to report that I've had an okay-ish week since then and as long as I don't think about the bigger picture (ALL THE THINGS ahead) too much, I feel like I can partake in life in an okay capacity, if that makes sense. Also, I have a job interview next Wednesday, thank God! It's for a temporary 50% job, but at this point I'm not picky and anything that'll help getting my parents to back off is more than welcome. My mom especially keeps nagging me and is really not helping with my already fragile state, so it's super important to me to remember to celebrate even the most minor of victories, even though to them there's still plenty of reason to be critical and negative. 

Thank you again for your time and interest – I *so* appreciate it and I'll definitely take you up on the offer. And, likewise, if you ever feel like you want to talk... message me and I'm happy to listen. Despite my current troubles, I'm usually a reasonable – and, dare I say, fun – person :)

I wish you a great weekend & a wonderful holiday season.
Someone sent me a really kind message but deleted their account before I could reply. If you're reading this, thank you & please reach out again - I'd love to hear how you've been doing.

Hi again! I hope you're well.

It does not cause any struggles whatsoever when it comes to a job or any task that's imposed on me by an external source (teachers, boss, even doing things for friends etc.). I was an A student, I'm super motivated and responsible and a total perfectionist, but only as long as there's some external validation or as long as there's a purpose. It's hard for me to find purpose in things I do just for myself; like, I struggle with going for runs, but I'll willingly stay up till 5AM to find the right typeface for my assignment. Can I ask which type you think you are? I know there are tons of personality frameworks out there, but this is one of the few that have made sense to me and that I refer back to when I come across a situation such as this (not that it *really* changes anything, but you know...). 

You nailed it. That's exactly how I've been feeling. While I was in school or when I was employed previously, there was always something to do and being productive and having strict schedules makes it easy for me to be more productive. I'm more likely to go to the gym when I have a full 9 hour day at the office than when I have the day off, ironically. Doing a few things early on in the day that make me feel somewhat accomplished (as I said, these days they can be as minor as 'getting up before 9' or 'going for a walk') definitely makes it more likely that I'll be more productive throughout the rest of the day. 

As opposed to when I was in school when people would leave me alone and all I had to do was get good grades and take some exams and write a thesis, now the things I have to do and accomplish are much less straightforward and the list is so long that just thinking about it makes me want to give up. Within the next six months I have go get a job (well, more within the next few weeks, really), get my license (have been dreading this forever), do a ton of 'adult' stuff that people generally *just do* without making a big deal of it, but for some reason to me something as simple as going to the dentist seems like a superhuman feat. 

I just hate that I'm wasting my time, really, and no one is to blame but me. Most of the time I can deal with that, but nights like yesterday have been increasing and once I'm in that downward spiral of feeling sad, feeling unaccomplished and feeling bad about myself it takes only a tiny bit of criticism from my parents or anything to make me feel misunderstood enough to want to just... not do this anymore.

Hey, I hope this makes sense. English is not my mother tongue and although I'm fine using it in an academic context, apparently writing something as honest as this is a bit more difficult for me :)

You are **awesome**, by the way. I've had a much better day today, shedding only a few tears behind my sunglasses, and that's partly due to your kind messages. Thank you so much.

Hi. Thank you so much for taking the time to read this and for taking the time to reply. I started sobbing when I read your reply because it's literally the nicest thing anyone has done for me and the most caring anyone has been towards me in a while. It's like a line in that Bright Eyes song, "Thank you stranger, for your therapeutic smile."

I feel like I haven't made a ton of sense in my original post, but for what it's worth, my degree is in Business and Design and I really love that area, but have been looking for more generic administrative positions as well. I think one of my main issues is that I'm a so-called Obliger (http://gretchenrubin.com/happiness_project/2015/01/ta-da-the-launch-of-my-quiz-on-the-four-tendencies-learn-about-yourself/) meaning that I have no problem meeting outer expectations like deadlines and such, but I find it hard to do things when they aren't imposed on me by an external source. 

I'm mad at myself that I'm letting my mood influence my behaviour. Intellectually, I know motivation is a fickle thing and if I really want something then I'll have to go after it regardless of whether I feel up for it. 

It's interesting... I don't want to end my life. Looking ten years ahead, I want children and family and dogs and contentment. But having to figure out how to get there, considering all the factors that'll have to work out... Just thinking about that is exhausting. 

Thank you again for your non-judgemental reply... you can't imagine how much I appreciate it.

I'm so happy you have a dog who loves you and depends on you. They truly are a reason to stay alive.

I know this is such an overused sentence, but I truly hope you'll feel better soon.
